六级大纲词汇 · 12英文原文

The Voice Behind the Curtain

帘子后面的声音 · 590 词 · 6 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A museum planned to unveil a restored portrait. The canvas depicted a girl in a velvet outfit with a miniature trumpet. Visitors admired the intricate embroidery and the portrait's aesthetics. The curator called the pose an embodiment of Renaissance glamour. Sam, a student organizing the performance, found a bronze clasp bearing the emblem on the girl's sleeve. It had been kept with a note about a choir. What looked like an exquisite accessory might connect the painting to a performer rather than to an aristocratic patron. The note came from a prestigious private salon known for showcasing musicians.

2At a pottery workshop Sam found a ceramic plate with the same mark. A carving on its rim showed a choir behind a curtain and a child holding a prop. A film reel from a retrospective contained the only surviving testimony. In it a man began to hum a melodious tune. He recalled a flood that had driven the musicians out of the theatre. A child continued a solo without the instruments. Her melody ended in an unusual chord, with a short vocal line from the bass.

3Sam asked the choir to rehearse it. At the first rehearsal, its grand tempo sounded like a symphony. The museum wanted a dazzling debut and asked for a spotlight on the glittering outfit. Sam listened to the reel again. A lyrical passage asked people to climb a hill before the water reached the door. A slow rendition made that lyric clear. He stitched a plain curtain and removed an imitation ivory fringe that distracted from the singer.

4At a small symposium a critic called the result a strange fusion of genres. He expected a spectacular launch and wanted the sound to animate a panoramic projection. Sam tried the arrangement. It turned the performance into a spectacle. One animated sequence added a comic scene. Sam found the animation distracting. Sam replaced it with a slow shot of the empty doorway. Then he let the choir sing unseen. A contemplative pause before the final chord made the room seem to hold its breath. The story could unfold without another prop. It evoked the wait described on the reel. The critic said the simpler version had a different aesthetic and agreed to give it a chance.

5At the opening visitors heard the recording before the live version began. The museum arranged a showcase for the clasp and plate, with a photograph of a sculpture above the old door. The three objects showed how local handicraft had helped preserve the song. The caption described the artifact. The depiction could evoke an event without identifying the girl. A visitor offered an impromptu, sentimental reminiscence. Her grandmother sang a verse reminiscent of it during power cuts. Sam had wanted a performance that would emulate the original. Her memory let him see how it could embody a sentiment the painting alone did not show. He did not need to put the costume in the limelight.

6Modest acclaim led to a revival of the song in the choir's repertoire. The song gained some renown. A renowned conductor heard it. He asked them to perform it without the costume. Sam kept the plain curtain and gave him a copy of the melody. Months later he heard the first chord through a door while the singers were warming up. He did not see the girl, the trumpet, or any of the scenery. He remembered them in the order in which he had found them. The performance had given the portrait a sound he could recall.

帘子后面的声音

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1博物馆准备公开一幅修复过的肖像。画里的女孩穿着天鹅绒衣服，手持一支小号。人们欣赏细密的刺绣和画面呈现的美感。策展人说，她的姿势体现了文艺复兴的华美。负责组织演出的学生萨姆发现一枚青铜搭扣，上面有与女孩袖子相同的徽记。搭扣和一张提到合唱团的便笺放在一起。那件精致的配饰可能与一名表演者有关。便笺来自一间常为音乐家举办演出的知名私人沙龙。

2萨姆在一家陶艺工坊找到一只带有相同标记的瓷盘。盘边的雕刻画着帘幕后的一群歌手和一个手拿道具的孩子。一卷后来回顾演出时拍的影片，是仅存的口述记录。片中，一位男子哼起一段悦耳的曲调。他说，那次洪水迫使乐手离开剧场，一个孩子却在没有乐器的情况下继续独唱。旋律以一个特别的和弦收尾，末尾还有一小段男低音。

3萨姆请合唱团排练。第一次排练时，他们用一种很庄重的节奏来唱，像在演奏交响曲。博物馆想要一次华丽的首演，还要求用聚光灯照亮闪闪发光的服装。萨姆重新听了录像。歌词像诗一样，请人们在水漫到门口前爬上山坡。放慢唱，就能听清那句词。他缝了一块素色帘子，拆掉会分散听众注意的仿象牙流苏。

4一场小型研讨会上，有评论家觉得这样的题材混搭有点怪。他想要气派的开场，希望声音给全景投影带来生气。萨姆试了一次，演出变成了热闹的场面。其中一段动画又加了个滑稽场景，萨姆觉得喧宾夺主，便换成空门口的慢镜头。接下来，合唱团在帘子后面唱。最后一个和弦前的沉静停顿，仿佛让整个屋子屏住了呼吸。不再添道具，故事也能继续。那一刻唤起了影片中人们等待的感觉。评论家也感受到简朴版本的美，愿意试试看。

5开幕时，观众先听录音，再听现场演出。博物馆把搭扣和瓷盘摆进展示柜，还放了一张旧剧场门上雕塑的照片。这三样东西让人看见当地手艺怎样留下了关于这首歌的记忆。图注说明了文物来历。画里的情景能唤起联想，却不足以确认女孩的身份。一位观众当场说起一段温情的往事，她的祖母在停电时唱过一段很像的歌词。萨姆原本想把演出做得和当年一样。听完她的回忆，他发现演出可以表达画本身传达不了的情感，服装也就不必摆在最显眼的地方。

6演出得到一些好评，合唱团把这首歌重新列入曲目。它渐渐有了些名气。一位知名指挥听到后，请他们不用戏服再唱一次。萨姆留下素色帘子，把曲谱抄了一份送给他。几个月后，歌手在屋里热嗓，萨姆隔着门听见第一个和弦。女孩、小号和布景都没出现在眼前，他却能按自己发现它们的顺序一一想起来。演出给这幅画留下了一段他还能回忆起来的声音。
